def _fmt_B(B):
    if B == 0:      return "0 T"
    if B >= 0.1:    return f"{B:.4f} T"
    if B >= 1e-4:   return f"{B*1e3:.4f} mT"
    return              f"{B*1e6:.2f} µT"


def draw_ext_field_on_lattice(ax, xs, ys, B_ext, phi_ext_deg,
                              needle_len, B_ext_max=None, B_signed=None,
                              color='#FFD700'):
    """Represents the external field in the image."""
    b_val = B_signed if B_signed is not None else B_ext
    
    B_max_ref = B_ext_max if (B_ext_max and B_ext_max > 0) else max(abs(b_val), 1e-30)
    
    if B_signed is not None:
        frac = (B_signed / B_max_ref + 1.0) / 2.0
    else:
        frac = min(abs(B_ext) / B_max_ref, 1.0)
    frac = max(0.0, min(frac, 1.0))
    field_on  = (abs(b_val) > 1e-30)

    # ── 2. panel field (ALWAYS visible) — corner upper right ──────
    xlim  = ax.get_xlim()
    ylim  = ax.get_ylim()
    xspan = xlim[1] - xlim[0]
    yspan = ylim[1] - ylim[0]

    bar_w = 0.20 * xspan
    bar_h = 0.018 * yspan
    arrow_zone_w = 0.07 * xspan

    box_w = bar_w + arrow_zone_w
    px = xlim[1] - 0.02 * xspan - box_w
    py_top = ylim[1] - 0.035 * yspan

    pad = needle_len * 0.25
    box_h = 0.140 * yspan + pad

    # semi-transparent background box
    ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle(
        (px - pad * 0.3, py_top - box_h),
        box_w + pad, box_h,
        facecolor='#080818', edgecolor=color,
        linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.82, zorder=19,
        transform=ax.transData))

    # ── text: intensity and direction ────────────
    if abs(b_val) > 1e-12:
        sign_str = "+" if b_val >= 0 else "-"
        b_str = sign_str + _fmt_B(abs(b_val))
    else:
        b_str = "0 T  (desligado)" if not field_on else "0 T"
    phi_str = f"dir: {phi_ext_deg:.1f} graus"

    text_color = color if field_on else '#777777'
    
    # Label "B ext" (left)
    ax.text(px, py_top - 0.022 * yspan, "B ext", color=color, fontsize=7,
            alpha=0.8, fontfamily='monospace', ha='left', va='top', zorder=23,
            transform=ax.transData)
            
    # Field value (second line)
    ax.text(px, py_top - 0.048 * yspan, b_str, color=text_color,
            fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', fontfamily='monospace',
            ha='left', va='top', zorder=23, transform=ax.transData)
            
    # Direction (third line)
    ax.text(px, py_top - 0.072 * yspan, phi_str, color=text_color,
            fontsize=7, fontfamily='monospace', ha='left', va='top', zorder=23,
            transform=ax.transData)

    # ── horizontal intensity bar ───
    bar_y = py_top - 0.115 * yspan
    ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle(
        (px, bar_y), bar_w, bar_h,
        facecolor='#252540', edgecolor='none',
        zorder=20, transform=ax.transData))
    
    # Active bar (centered, growing left for negative fields and right for positive fields)
    f = b_val / B_max_ref if B_max_ref > 0 else 0.0
    f = max(-1.0, min(f, 1.0))
    center_x = px + bar_w / 2.0
    
    if abs(f) > 0.001:
        if f >= 0.0:
            fill_x = center_x
            fill_w = (bar_w / 2.0) * f
        else:
            fill_w = (bar_w / 2.0) * abs(f)
            fill_x = center_x - fill_w
            
        ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle(
            (fill_x, bar_y), fill_w, bar_h,
            facecolor=color if field_on else '#555555',
            edgecolor='none', alpha=0.85, zorder=21,
            transform=ax.transData))
            
    ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle(
        (px, bar_y), bar_w, bar_h,
        facecolor='none', edgecolor='#5A5A8A',
        linewidth=0.7, zorder=22, transform=ax.transData))

    # Red vertical center line (representing zero field reference)
    ax.plot([center_x, center_x], [bar_y, bar_y + bar_h],
            color='#FF0000' if field_on else '#777777',
            linewidth=1.2, zorder=23, transform=ax.transData)

    # ── direction dial (circle + arrow): centered next to the text lines ──
    arrow_cx = px + box_w - pad - 0.01 * xspan
    arrow_cy = py_top - 0.048 * yspan
    r_dial   = needle_len * 0.55 * 1.30
    
    dial = plt.Circle((arrow_cx, arrow_cy), r_dial, facecolor='#080818',
                      edgecolor='#5A5A8A', lw=0.7, zorder=20)
    ax.add_patch(dial)
    
    f = b_val / B_max_ref if B_max_ref > 0 else 0.0
    f = max(-1.0, min(f, 1.0))
    
    if field_on and abs(f) > 1e-5:
        phi_arrow = (phi_ext_deg + 180.0) % 360.0 if f < 0 else phi_ext_deg
        # Scale arrow length: full diameter at |f|=1, shrinks toward center
        arrow_len = abs(f) * (2.0 * r_dial)

        cos_a = np.cos(np.deg2rad(phi_arrow))
        sin_a = np.sin(np.deg2rad(phi_arrow))

        # Arrow geometry (centered in the circle) - scaled proportionally to |f| to preserve aspect ratio
        scale_w = abs(f)
        shaft_w  = (r_dial * 0.28) * scale_w          # shaft half-width
        head_w   = (r_dial * 0.60) * scale_w          # head half-width
        head_len = (r_dial * 0.65) * scale_w          # head length

        # Tail position (centered on arrow_cx/cy)
        x_tail = arrow_cx - (arrow_len / 2.0) * cos_a
        y_tail = arrow_cy - (arrow_len / 2.0) * sin_a

        from matplotlib.patches import FancyArrow
        fat_arrow = FancyArrow(
            x_tail, y_tail,
            arrow_len * cos_a, arrow_len * sin_a,
            width=shaft_w * 2,
            head_width=head_w * 2,
            head_length=head_len,
            length_includes_head=True,
            facecolor=color,
            edgecolor='#1A1A2E',
            linewidth=0.8,
            zorder=22,
            transform=ax.transData,
        )
        ax.add_patch(fat_arrow)

    # ── 1. arrows at the sites ─────────────────
    if field_on:
        phi_inst = np.deg2rad(phi_ext_deg + 180.0 if b_val < 0 else phi_ext_deg)
        cos_phi  = np.cos(phi_inst)
        sin_phi  = np.sin(phi_inst)
        alen_sites = needle_len * 0.35
        dx_a = alen_sites * cos_phi
        dy_a = alen_sites * sin_phi
        N, M = xs.shape
        x0 = xs.ravel() - dx_a / 2.0
        y0 = ys.ravel() - dy_a / 2.0
        ax.quiver(x0, y0, dx_a, dy_a,
                 angles='xy', scale_units='xy', scale=1.0,
                 color=color, alpha=0.50, width=0.0035,
                 headwidth=4.0, headlength=4.5, headaxislength=4.0,
                 zorder=2)


def draw_halos_batch(ax, xs, ys, thetas, needle_len, r_halo=None,
                     halo_mode='order', domain_tol_deg=15.0):
    N, M = thetas.shape
    _r = r_halo if r_halo is not None else needle_len * 0.58
    _n_domains_found = None
    _n_significant   = None

    if halo_mode == 'domains':
        domain_labels, _n_domains_found = label_magnetic_domains(
            thetas, tol_deg=domain_tol_deg)
        K_total = N * M
        _unique_labels, _inverse, _counts = np.unique(
            domain_labels, return_inverse=True, return_counts=True)
        _inverse = _inverse.ravel()
        _min_domain_size = max(3, int(0.02 * K_total))
        _is_significant = _counts >= _min_domain_size
        _n_significant = int(np.sum(_is_significant))

        _sig_idx = np.where(_is_significant)[0]
        _sig_order = _sig_idx[np.argsort(-_counts[_sig_idx])]
        _color_rank = np.full(len(_unique_labels), -1, dtype=int)
        _color_rank[_sig_order] = np.arange(len(_sig_order))

        palette = _domain_color_palette(max(_n_significant, 1))
        _gray = np.array([0.45, 0.45, 0.48, 1.0])
        per_label_colors = np.tile(_gray, (len(_unique_labels), 1))
        if _n_significant > 0:
            per_label_colors[_sig_order] = palette[:_n_significant]

        colors = per_label_colors[_inverse]
    else:
        align_sum   = np.zeros((N, M))
        align_count = np.zeros((N, M))
        for di, dj in [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]:
            dst_i0, dst_i1 = max(0, -di), N - max(0, di)
            dst_j0, dst_j1 = max(0, -dj), M - max(0, dj)
            src_i0, src_i1 = dst_i0 + di, dst_i1 + di
            src_j0, src_j1 = dst_j0 + dj, dst_j1 + dj
            delta = thetas[dst_i0:dst_i1, dst_j0:dst_j1] - thetas[src_i0:src_i1, src_j0:src_j1]
            align_sum[dst_i0:dst_i1, dst_j0:dst_j1]   += np.cos(delta)
            align_count[dst_i0:dst_i1, dst_j0:dst_j1] += 1.0

        align_avg = np.where(align_count > 0, align_sum / np.maximum(align_count, 1.0), 0.0)
        colors = cm.RdYlGn((align_avg.ravel() + 1.0) / 2.0)

    halo_patches = [plt.Circle((x, y), _r)
                    for x, y in zip(xs.ravel(), ys.ravel())]
    _halo_alpha = 0.35 if halo_mode == 'domains' else 0.20
    pc_halos = PatchCollection(
        halo_patches, facecolor=colors, edgecolor='none',
        alpha=_halo_alpha, zorder=1)
    ax.add_collection(pc_halos)
    return _n_domains_found, _n_significant


def plot_state(thetas, xs, ys, title="Array of compass", show_order=True,
               needle_len=0.42, needle_width=0.10, r_halo=None,
               B_ext=0.0, phi_ext_deg=0.0, B_ext_max=None,
               B_signed=None, figsize_inches=None,
               halo_mode='order', domain_tol_deg=15.0):
    """Generates a figure with the instantaneous state of the needle lattice."""
    if figsize_inches is None:
        x_span = xs.max() - xs.min() + 2 * needle_len * 2.0
        y_span = ys.max() - ys.min() + 2 * needle_len * 4.0
        aspect = x_span / y_span if y_span > 0 else 1.0
        base = 8.0
        if aspect >= 1.0:
            fig_w = min(base * aspect, 20.0)
            fig_h = fig_w / aspect
        else:
            fig_h = min(base / aspect, 20.0)
            fig_w = fig_h * aspect
        figsize_inches = (max(fig_w, 6.0), max(fig_h, 6.0))

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize_inches, facecolor='#1A1A2E')
    ax.set_facecolor('#16213E')
    N, M = thetas.shape

    if show_order:
        _n_domains_found, _n_significant = draw_halos_batch(
            ax, xs, ys, thetas, needle_len, r_halo=r_halo,
            halo_mode=halo_mode, domain_tol_deg=domain_tol_deg)

    draw_compass_batch(ax, xs, ys, thetas,
                       length=needle_len, width=needle_width)

    ax.set_aspect('equal')
    margin = needle_len * 1.6
    yspan_lattice = ys.max() - ys.min() + 2 * margin
    yspan = yspan_lattice / 0.8
    ax.set_xlim(xs.min() - margin, xs.max() + margin)
    ax.set_ylim(ys.min() - margin, ys.min() - margin + yspan)
    ax.set_title(title, color='#ECF0F1', fontsize=11, pad=10,
                 fontfamily='monospace')
    ax.tick_params(colors='#7F8C8D')
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_edgecolor('#2C3E50')

    draw_ext_field_on_lattice(ax, xs, ys, B_ext, phi_ext_deg, needle_len,
                              B_ext_max=B_ext_max, B_signed=B_signed)

    patch_n = mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#FFFFFF', edgecolor='#555',
                              label='North Pole (white)')
    patch_s = mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#2E6DB4', edgecolor='#555',
                              label='South Pole (blue)')
    handles = [patch_n, patch_s]
    if show_order and halo_mode == 'domains':
        if _n_significant < _n_domains_found:
            _dom_label = (f'Domains: {_n_significant} main '
                          f'(+{_n_domains_found - _n_significant} small, grey)  '
                          f'tol={domain_tol_deg:.0f}°')
        else:
            _dom_label = f'Magnetic Domains: {_n_domains_found}  (tol={domain_tol_deg:.0f}°)'
        patch_dom = mpatches.Patch(facecolor='none', edgecolor='none',
                                   label=_dom_label)
        handles.append(patch_dom)
    if B_ext > 0:
        patch_b = mpatches.Patch(facecolor='#FFD700', edgecolor='#555',
                                  label=f'Ext. Field.  {_fmt_B(B_ext)}  '
                                        f'φ={phi_ext_deg:.1f}°')
        handles.append(patch_b)
    ax.legend(handles=handles, loc='lower left',
              facecolor='#1A1A2E', edgecolor='#2C3E50',
              labelcolor='#ECF0F1', fontsize=8)

    return fig, ax


# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 8. RELAXATION ANIMATION
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def animate_relaxation(thetas_hist, xs, ys,
                       needle_len=0.42, needle_width=0.10,
                       B_ext=0.0, phi_ext_deg=0.0,
                       interval=80, save_gif=None):
    """Generates a frame-by-frame animation of the lattice time evolution."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 7), facecolor='#1A1A2E')
    ax.set_facecolor('#16213E')
    ax.set_aspect('equal')
    margin = needle_len * 1.6
    yspan_lattice = ys.max() - ys.min() + 2 * margin
    yspan = yspan_lattice / 0.8
    ax.set_xlim(xs.min() - margin, xs.max() + margin)
    ax.set_ylim(ys.min() - margin, ys.min() - margin + yspan)

    N, M = thetas_hist[0].shape

    def update(frame):
        for art in ax.lines + ax.patches + ax.collections:
            art.remove()
        thetas = thetas_hist[frame]
        draw_compass_batch(ax, xs, ys, thetas,
                           length=needle_len, width=needle_width)
        draw_ext_field_on_lattice(ax, xs, ys, B_ext, phi_ext_deg, needle_len)
        ax.set_title(f"Dipolar relaxation — step {frame * 20}",
                     color='#ECF0F1', fontsize=11, fontfamily='monospace')
        return []

    ani = FuncAnimation(fig, update, frames=len(thetas_hist),
                        interval=interval, blit=False)
    if save_gif:
        ani.save(save_gif, writer='pillow', fps=12, dpi=90)
        _print(f"GIF saved at: {save_gif}")
    return fig, ani

# 9. GLOBAL ORDER-PARAMETER PLOT
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def plot_order_parameter(thetas_hist, outpath, dt=None):
    """Plots the time evolution of the global magnetic order parameter S(t)."""
    order_params = [
        np.abs(np.mean(np.exp(1j * th)))
        for th in thetas_hist
    ]

    if dt is not None:
        time_ax = np.arange(len(order_params)) * 20 * dt
        xlabel  = "Time  t  [s]"
    else:
        time_ax = np.arange(len(order_params))
        xlabel  = "Snapshot (every 20 steps)"

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.5), facecolor='#1A1A2E')
    ax.set_facecolor('#0F3460')
    ax.plot(time_ax, order_params, color='#E94560', lw=2)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel, color='#BDC3C7')
    ax.set_ylabel(r"Order parameter $S = |\langle e^{i\theta}\rangle|$",
                  color='#BDC3C7')
    ax.set_title("Global Magnetic Order Parameter Evolution",
                 color='#ECF0F1', fontfamily='monospace')
    ax.tick_params(colors='#7F8C8D')
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.05)
    ax.grid(True, color='#2C3E50', alpha=0.5)
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_edgecolor('#2C3E50')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(outpath, dpi=130, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='#1A1A2E')
    _print(f"Order parameter saved at: {outpath}")

# 10. COMMAND-LINE INTERFACE (main)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def main():
    """Command-line entry point of the simulation."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Simulation of a compass-needle array — 2D dipolar field",
        formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter)

    grp = parser.add_argument_group("Lattice geometry")
    grp.add_argument('--N', type=int, default=8,
                     help='Number of needle ROWS')
    grp.add_argument('--M', type=int, default=8,
                     help='Number of needle COLUMNS')
    grp.add_argument('--R', type=float, default=0.025,
                     help='Radius of the circumscribed circle enclosing each needle [m]. '
                           'The distance between neighbor centers = 2R. '
                           'Default: 0.025 m = 2.5 cm')
    grp.add_argument('--needle_frac', type=float, default=0.80,
                     help='Needle length as a fraction of the diameter 2R '
                           '(0.0 to 0.8). Default: 0.80  ->  needle = 0.80 * 2R. '
                           'Values outside the range will be clamped.')
    grp.add_argument('--geometry',
                     choices=['square', 'triangular', 'honeycomb'],
                     default='square',
                     help='Lattice geometry type')

    grp2 = parser.add_argument_group("Physics and simulation")
    grp2.add_argument('--moment', type=float, default=None,
                      help='Magnetic moment of each needle [A·m²]. '
                           'If omitted (default), calculated automatically '
                           'from the physical volume of the needle (R, '
                           'needle_frac, thickness), assuming that the steel '
                           'is saturated along the long axis (North) '
                           'of the needle: m = Ms * volume, where Ms is the '
                           'saturation magnetization of the steel (--steel_Bsat). '
                           'If supplied explicitly, this value '
                           'overrides the automatic calculation. '
                           'Typical: 0.01 (small) to 1.0 (large).')
    grp2.add_argument('--inertia', type=float, default=None,
                      help='Moment of inertia of each needle [kg·m²]. '
                           'If omitted (default), calculated automatically '
                           'from the physical geometry of the needle (R, '
                           'needle_frac, thickness) as a steel plate: '
                           'I = (1/12)*mass*(L^2 + width^2), '
                           'mass = density * L * width * thickness. '
                           'If supplied explicitly, this value '
                           'overrides the automatic calculation.')
    grp2.add_argument('--needle_thickness', type=float,
                      default=NEEDLE_THICKNESS_DEFAULT,
                      help='Thickness of the steel sheet of the needle [m], '
                           'used in the automatic calculations of the moment of '
                           'inertia and the magnetic moment (when '
                           '--inertia / --moment are not provided). '
                           f'Default: {NEEDLE_THICKNESS_DEFAULT*1e3:.2f} mm')
    grp2.add_argument('--steel_density', type=float,
                      default=STEEL_DENSITY_DEFAULT,
                      help='Density of the magnetic steel [kg/m³], used '
                           'only in the automatic calculation of the moment of '
                           'inertia. Default: {STEEL_DENSITY_DEFAULT:.0f} '
                           'kg/m³ (standard carbon steel)')
    grp2.add_argument('--steel_Bsat', type=float,
                      default=None,
                      help='Saturation flux density of the magnetic '
                           'steel [T], used only in the automatic '
                           'calculation of the magnetic moment (when '
                           '--moment is not provided). Relation: '
                           'Ms = Bsat / mu0. Typical range for standard '
                           'magnetic steels: 1.6-2.2 T. '
                           f'Default: {STEEL_MS_SATURATION_DEFAULT*4*np.pi*1e-7:.2f} T')
    grp2.add_argument('--damping', type=float, default=DAMPING_DEFAULT,
                      help='Viscous air damping coefficient b [N·m·s/rad]. '
                           'Zero = no damping (oscillates indefinitely). '
                           'Large = no visible oscillations. '
                           f'Default: {DAMPING_DEFAULT:.2e} N·m·s/rad '
                           '(underdamped, Q >> 1)')
    grp2.add_argument('--damping_noise', type=float, default=0.0,
                      help='Relative noise amplitude for per-needle damping. '
                           'Damping for each needle is randomized as b_i = max(0, b * (1 + noise * U[-1, 1])). '
                           'Default: 0.0 (no noise).')
    grp2.add_argument('--t_sim', type=float, default=2.0,
                      help='Total physical simulation time [s] '
                           '(= sum of integrated dt steps). '
                           'In hysteresis: covers 1 full cycle (0->Hmax->-Hmax->Hmax). '
                           'In sine: must cover several periods (>= 3/field_freq). '
                           'Default: 2.0 s')
    grp2.add_argument('--t_sim_full', type=int, default=0, choices=[0, 1],
                      help='1 = runs until the END of t_sim, disabling all '
                           'early physical stop criteria (S=1.00, '
                           'lattice at rest, torque equilibrium in '
                           'pulse/step modes). Useful for uniform time-series '
                           'lengths in sweeps. User interruptions '
                           '(Ctrl+I/Ctrl+C) remain active. '
                           '0 (default) = normal early stops.')
    grp2.add_argument('--field_mode',
                      choices=['static', 'hysteresis', 'sine', 'pulse',
                               'step_pos', 'step_neg', 'forc'],
                      default='static',
                      help='External field mode')
    grp2.add_argument('--forc_n_curves', type=int, default=30,
                      help='Number of first-order reversal curves (FORCs) to simulate (default: 30).')
    grp2.add_argument('--forc_Br_min', type=float, default=None,
                      help='Minimum reversal field Br_min [T] (default: -B_ext_mag).')
    grp2.add_argument('--forc_t_sat', type=float, default=None,
                      help='Saturation hold time [s] per cycle (default: 0.05 s).')
    grp2.add_argument('--forc_t_ramp_down', type=float, default=None,
                      help='Time to ramp down from saturation to reversal field [s] per cycle (default: 0.10 s).')
    grp2.add_argument('--forc_t_ramp_up', type=float, default=None,
                      help='Time to sweep back from reversal field to saturation [s] per cycle (default: 0.20 s).')
    grp2.add_argument('--hyst_spacing', choices=['linear', 'log'],
                      default='linear',
                      help='Hysteresis ramp spacing')
    grp2.add_argument('--hyst_log_k', type=float, default=5.0,
                      help='Concentration parameter of log spacing for hysteresis')
    grp2.add_argument('--field_delay', type=float, default=0.0,
                      help='Delay t_delay [s]')
    grp2.add_argument('--t_pulse', type=float, default=None,
                      help='Pulse duration [s]')
    grp2.add_argument('--torque_tol', type=float, default=1e-3,
                      help='Relative torque tolerance for equilibrium stopping criterion')
    grp2.add_argument('--field_freq', type=float, default=1.0,
                      help='Frequency of the sinusoidal field [Hz].')
    grp2.add_argument('--dt_factor', type=float, default=0.05,
                      help='Fraction of natural period T0 used as time step dt')
    grp2.add_argument('--noise', type=float, default=1.5,
                      help='Initial random noise amplitude in orientations [rad]')
    grp2.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=42,
                      help='Random generator seed')
    grp2.add_argument('--pbc', type=int, choices=[0, 1], default=0,
                      help='Periodic boundary conditions (PBC)')
    grp2.add_argument('--pbc_images', type=int, default=1,
                      help='Number of periodic shell replicas summed')
    grp2.add_argument('--gpu', type=int, choices=[0, 1], default=0,
                      help='Enable GPU acceleration (CuPy)')
    grp2.add_argument('--progress_bar', type=int, choices=[0, 1], default=1,
                      help='Show interactive progress bar in real time')
    grp2.add_argument('--halo_mode', type=str, choices=['order', 'domains'],
                      default='order',
                      help='Halo coloring mode')
    grp2.add_argument('--domain_tol', type=float, default=15.0,
                      help='Angular tolerance [degrees] for domain grouping')

    grp3 = parser.add_argument_group("Uniform external field (SI)")
    grp3.add_argument('--B_ext', type=float, default=0.0,
                      help='External field intensity [T].')
    grp3.add_argument('--phi_ext', type=float, default=0.0,
                      help='External field direction [degrees]')
    grp3.add_argument('--ext_Bx', type=float, default=None,
                      help='Bx component of the external field [T]')
    grp3.add_argument('--ext_By', type=float, default=None,
                      help='By component of the external field [T]')

    grp4 = parser.add_argument_group("Output")
    grp4.add_argument('--video', type=str, default=None,
                      metavar='NAME',
                      help='Generate MP4 video with this base name.')
    grp4.add_argument('--frame_every', type=int, default=5,
                      help='Save one frame every N steps.')
    grp4.add_argument('--make_images', type=int, default=1, choices=[0, 1],
                      help='1 (default) = generate summary PNG images, 0 = disable.')
    grp4.add_argument('--fps', type=int, default=24,
                      help='Frames per second of the MP4 video.')
    grp4.add_argument('--dpi', type=int, default=120,
                      help='Frame resolution in DPI.')
    grp4.add_argument('--keep_frames', action='store_true',
                      help='Keep the temporary folder of PNG frames')
    grp4.add_argument('--hyst_autoscale', type=int, choices=[0, 1], default=0,
                      help='Enables automatic scaling (autoscale) of the axes for the MxH hysteresis curve.')
    grp4.add_argument('--csv_order', choices=['t', 'B'], default='t',
                      help='Column order in the exported CSV file.')
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.needle_frac < 0.0 or args.needle_frac > 0.8:
        clamped = max(0.0, min(args.needle_frac, 0.8))
        _print(f"  Warning: --needle_frac {args.needle_frac} outside range "
                f"[0, 0.8]; adjusted to {clamped}")
        args.needle_frac = clamped

    np.random.seed(args.seed)

    if args.ext_Bx is not None or args.ext_By is not None:
        Bext_x = args.ext_Bx if args.ext_Bx is not None else 0.0
        Bext_y = args.ext_By if args.ext_By is not None else 0.0
        B_ext_mag = np.sqrt(Bext_x**2 + Bext_y**2)
        phi_ext_deg = np.degrees(np.arctan2(Bext_y, Bext_x))
    else:
        phi_rad = np.deg2rad(args.phi_ext)
        Bext_x  = args.B_ext * np.cos(phi_rad)
        Bext_y  = args.B_ext * np.sin(phi_rad)
        B_ext_mag   = args.B_ext
        phi_ext_deg = args.phi_ext

    R          = args.R
    needle_len = args.needle_frac * 2.0 * R
    needle_width = needle_len * 0.22

    if args.inertia is None:
        inertia = compute_inertia_from_geometry(
            needle_len, needle_width, args.needle_thickness,
            density=args.steel_density)
        _inertia_auto = True
    else:
        inertia = args.inertia
        _inertia_auto = False

    if args.steel_Bsat is not None:
        _Ms_used = args.steel_Bsat / (4.0 * np.pi * 1e-7)
    else:
        _Ms_used = STEEL_MS_SATURATION_DEFAULT
    if args.moment is None:
        moment = compute_moment_from_geometry(
            needle_len, needle_width, args.needle_thickness, Ms=_Ms_used)
        _moment_auto = True
    else:
        moment = args.moment
        _moment_auto = False

    def fmt_field(B):
        if B == 0:      return "0 T"
        if B >= 0.1:    return f"{B:.4f} T"
        if B >= 1e-4:   return f"{B*1e3:.4f} mT"
        return              f"{B*1e6:.2f} µT"

    _print(f"\n{'═'*62}")
    _print(f"  Version      : V68")
    _print(f"  Developer    : J.P. Sinnecker")
    if args.gpu and _GPU_AVAILABLE:
        try:
            _gpu_name = cp.cuda.runtime.getDeviceProperties(0)['name'].decode()
        except Exception:
            _gpu_name = "GPU CUDA"
        _print(f"  Backend      : GPU ({_gpu_name}) via CuPy  [--gpu 1]")
    elif args.gpu and not _GPU_AVAILABLE:
        _print(f"  Backend      : CPU (NumPy)  [--gpu 1 requested, but GPU unavailable]")
        if _GPU_ERROR_MSG:
            if 'CUDA headers' in _GPU_ERROR_MSG or 'CUDA_PATH' in _GPU_ERROR_MSG:
                _print(f"  GPU unavailable: missing CUDA Toolkit headers.")
                _print(f"  Solution: pip install cupy-cuda12x[ctk]")
            else:
                _print(f"  GPU unavailable: {_GPU_ERROR_MSG[:70]}")
        else:
            _print(f"  GPU unavailable: cupy not installed")
    else:
        _gpu_hint = " (GPU detected, use --gpu 1 to activate)" if _GPU_AVAILABLE else ""
        _print(f"  Backend      : CPU (NumPy)  [--gpu 0]{_gpu_hint}")
    _print(f"  Array        : {args.geometry}  {args.N}x{args.M} needles")
    pbc_str = (f"on  (n_images={args.pbc_images}, sum over "
               f"{(2*args.pbc_images+1)**2} cells)") if args.pbc else "off"
    _print(f"  PBC          : {pbc_str}")
    _print(f"  Radius R     : {args.R*100:.2f} cm  (2R = {2*args.R*100:.2f} cm)")
    _print(f"  Needle R     : {args.needle_frac*100:.0f}% of 2R = {args.needle_frac*2*args.R*100:.2f} cm")
    if _moment_auto:
        _Bsat_used = _Ms_used * 4.0 * np.pi * 1e-7
        _print(f"  Mag Moment.  : {moment:.4g} A.m2  per needle")
    else:
        _print(f"  Mag Moment.  : {moment:.4g} A.m2  per needle [manual value]")
    if _inertia_auto:
        _mass_g = args.steel_density * needle_len * needle_width * args.needle_thickness * 1e3
        _print(f"  Inertia      : {inertia:.3e} kg.m2  per needle")
    else:
        _print(f"  Inertia      : {inertia:.3e} kg.m2  per needle [manual value]")
    if args.damping_noise > 0.0:
        _print(f"  Damping      : {args.damping:.3e} N.m.s/rad  (air) [+/- {args.damping_noise*100:.1f}% noise]")
    else:
        _print(f"  Damping      : {args.damping:.3e} N.m.s/rad  (air)")
    _print(f"  External Field: {fmt_field(B_ext_mag)}  phi={phi_ext_deg:.1f} degrees")
    _print(f"  Components   : Bx={fmt_field(abs(Bext_x))}  By={fmt_field(abs(Bext_y))}")
    field_mode_str = args.field_mode
    _print(f"  Field Mode   : {field_mode_str}")
    _print(f"  Noise Seed   : {args.seed}")
    _print(f"{'═'*62}\n")

    xs, ys, thetas_init, nn_dist, Lx_period, Ly_period = make_grid(
        N=args.N, M=args.M,
        geometry=args.geometry,
        noise=args.noise,
        R=args.R,
    )

    r_halo     = R * 0.98
    cutoff     = nn_dist * 2.6

    if args.pbc:
        max_cutoff_pbc = min(Lx_period, Ly_period) / 2.0
        if cutoff > max_cutoff_pbc:
            _print(f"  PBC: cutoff reduced from {cutoff*100:.2f}cm to "
                    f"{max_cutoff_pbc*100:.2f}cm (min(Lx,Ly)/2 limit)")
            cutoff = max_cutoff_pbc

    B_ref = MU0_OVER_4PI * 2.0 * moment / nn_dist**3
    _print(f"  B_dipolar ref: {fmt_field(B_ref)}  (Between neighbours)")
    if B_ext_mag > 0:
        ratio = B_ext_mag / B_ref
        dom = "DOMINANT" if ratio > 1 else "weak"
        _print(f"  B_ext/B_ref  : {ratio:.3f}  (External Field - {dom})")
    _print()

    ext_kwargs = dict(B_ext=B_ext_mag, phi_ext_deg=phi_ext_deg,
                      r_halo=r_halo, halo_mode=args.halo_mode,
                      domain_tol_deg=args.domain_tol)

    _x_span = (xs.max() - xs.min()) + 4 * needle_len
    _y_span = (ys.max() - ys.min()) + 6 * needle_len
    _aspect = _x_span / _y_span if _y_span > 0 else 1.0
    _base   = 8.0
    if _aspect >= 1.0:
        _fw = min(_base * _aspect, 20.0)
        _fh = _fw / _aspect
    else:
        _fh = min(_base / _aspect, 20.0)
        _fw = _fh * _aspect
    figsize_main = (max(_fw, 6.0), max(_fh, 6.0))

    ext_kwargs['figsize_inches'] = figsize_main

    if args.make_images:
        fig0, _ = plot_state(thetas_init, xs, ys,
                             title="Initial state (random)",
                             needle_len=needle_len, needle_width=needle_width,
                             **ext_kwargs)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig("compass_initial.png",
                    dpi=args.dpi, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='#1A1A2E')
        plt.close(fig0)
        _print("Initial State Saved.")

    frame_dir   = None
    final_video = None
    if args.video and not args.make_images:
        _print(f"  Warning: --video '{args.video}' was requested along with "
               f"--make_images 0. Ignoring --video.")
        args.video = None

    if args.video:
        import os
        if not os.path.splitext(args.video)[1]:
            args.video = args.video + ".mp4"
        final_video = next_available_path(args.video)
        _print(f"  Video filename: '{final_video}'")
        base      = os.path.splitext(final_video)[0]
        frame_dir = base + "_frames"
        _print(f"Integrating and saving frames at '{frame_dir}/'...")
    else:
        _print("Integrating inertial dynamics...")

    thetas_eq, omegas_eq, thetas_hist, n_frames, sim_dt, stop_reason, field_log = relax(
        thetas_init.copy(), xs, ys,
        t_sim=args.t_sim,
        dt_factor=args.dt_factor,
        inertia=inertia,
        damping=args.damping,
        damping_noise=args.damping_noise,
        cutoff=cutoff,
        ext_field=(Bext_x, Bext_y),
        moment=moment,
        field_mode=args.field_mode,
        field_freq=args.field_freq,
        frame_dir=frame_dir,

# Walkthrough - FORC Measurement Protocol Implementation (V68)

This document summarizes the changes made to implement the First-Order Reversal Curve (FORC) measurement protocol in the compass lattice simulation.

## Changes Made

### 1. Version Bump
- Updated simulation version to **V68** in:
  - [compass.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/compass.py) (Header comment, CLI `--version` output, and log headers).
  - [compass_simV68.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/compass_simV68.py) (Frozen snapshot clone).

### 2. FORC Up-Sweep Phase and Loop Index Tracking
- In the main integration loop of the `relax()` function inside [compass.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/compass.py#L1228), implemented tracking for the up-sweep phase:
  - Calculated `t_local = t_now - k * T_cycle` (current elapsed time within the cycle `k`).
  - Identified the up-sweep segment using `is_up_sweep = (t_local > tsat + t_down)`.
  - Logged each step as a tuple with additional fields: `(t_now, B_scalar, M_proj, S_now, Br_curr, is_up_sweep, k)`.

### 3. Separation of Curves in Visualization
- Updated `_render_hyst_panel` (real-time rendering) and `_plot_hysteresis` (final plot generation) to:
  - Group logged data points by their loop index `k` using a dictionary of curves.
  - Render each loop segment as an independent line segment, preventing visual artifacts where lines connect back to the start of the next cycle.
  - Maintained the active marker (red dot) tracing the full continuous sweep in real time.

### 4. CSV Logging Filter
- Modified both the relaxation inner loop saving and the main CLI exit saving code in `compass.py`:
  - Enforced that only data points belonging to the up-sweep phase (`is_up_sweep == True`) are recorded in the exported files:
    - `forc_curve.csv`
    - `compass_field_log.csv`
  - Columns written: `['t_s', 'B_applied_T', 'M_proj', 'S', 'B_r']` (and `B_T` for `forc_curve.csv`).

### 5. Frozen Snapshot and Freeze Script
- Created [freeze_v68.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/freeze_v68.py) to snapshot this version.
- Created [compass_simV68.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/compass_simV68.py) as the frozen codebase.

---

## Verification Results

### Simulated Test Run
Due to macOS sandbox restrictions on subprocesses writing to the Dropbox folder, the test run was executed in the scratch sandbox directory `/Users/jps/.gemini/antigravity-ide/scratch/simbuild/` using the command:
```bash
/opt/anaconda3/bin/python3 compass.py --N 4 --M 4 --field_mode forc --forc_n_curves 5 --t_sim_full 1 --damping 8e-6
```

#### Results:
- **Simulation Run**: Successfully completed all 5 cycles without any numerical issues.
- **CSV Data Validation**: The exported CSV files contain exactly **73 lines** of up-sweep measurements instead of 127 total steps, validating that the down-sweeps were correctly filtered out.
- **Copy to Workspace**: The correct CSV files were successfully written to the workspace:
  - [forc_curve.csv](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/forc_curve.csv)
  - [compass_field_log.csv](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/compass_field_log.csv)

---

## Next Steps for the User
When you resume, run the simulation in your own local terminal to write the output plots and video files directly to the Dropbox folder:
```bash

```

# Implementation Plan — Cross-Platform Dropbox Environment Configuration

This plan details the implementation of a robust, cross-platform environment configuration to run the compass lattice simulation scripts (`compass.py` and sweeps) without any permission or file-locking problems when the project is hosted in a Dropbox (or other cloud-synced) directory on macOS, Linux, or Windows.

## The Problem

1. **macOS CloudStorage/FileProvider Sandboxing**: On macOS, directories under `~/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox` are managed by FileProvider. Subprocesses (like Python scripts executed inside an IDE terminal) often lack permission to write directly to these folders, raising `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`.
2. **Cloud Sync File Locking**: On Windows and Linux, Dropbox immediately locks files (plots, CSVs, or frames) the moment they are created or modified to sync them. If the Python script tries to open, write, or rename them at the same time, it crashes with `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied`.
3. **Dropbox Virtual Environment Syncing**: Storing virtual environments (`.venv`) inside Dropbox is a bad practice. It leads to syncing thousands of tiny dependency files, which degrades system performance, and virtual environments are OS-specific, meaning a synced virtual environment will crash on a different OS.

---

## Proposed Solution

We will create a standardized, automated setup and wrapper script suite:
1. **`setup_env.py`**: A cross-platform setup script that:
   - Detects the user's OS.
   - Installs dependencies (`numpy`, `matplotlib`) into a virtual environment stored **outside** the Dropbox directory (e.g. in `~/.compass_sim_venv/`) so that virtual environment files are never synced.
   - Generates local shell script wrappers (`run.sh` for Mac/Linux and `run.bat` for Windows) to run the simulation using this local venv.
2. **`run_safely.py`**: A robust wrapper that runs Python simulation code in a local temporary directory (e.g., `/tmp` or `%TEMP%`) and copies the output files back. This completely bypasses macOS sandboxing errors and Dropbox file sync locks during simulation execution.
3. **Detailed Setup Guide**: Instructions for system-level settings (such as macOS Full Disk Access).

---

## Proposed Changes

### Configuration & Dependency Setup

#### [NEW] [requirements.txt](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/requirements.txt)
- Define standard packages: `numpy` and `matplotlib`.

#### [NEW] [setup_env.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/setup_env.py)
- Automatically verify Python 3.
- Locate the home directory and create a virtual environment (`.compass_sim_venv`) outside of the Dropbox folder.
- Install packages from `requirements.txt`.
- Generate local scripts in the workspace:
  - `run.sh` (for Mac/Linux)
  - `run.bat` (for Windows)
- Mark `run.sh` as executable (`chmod +x`).

---

### Execution Wrapper

#### [NEW] [run_safely.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/run_safely.py)
- Accepts the script name and any arguments (e.g., `python3 run_safely.py compass.py --field_mode forc`).
- Creates a temporary directory outside Dropbox.
- Copies the simulation script to the temporary directory.
- Executes the simulation script using `subprocess` in the temporary directory.
- Copies output files (`.png`, `.csv`, `.mp4`) back to the Dropbox folder.
- Handles `PermissionError` during copy operations by offering detailed OS-specific advice (like Full Disk Access instructions) or writing to a fallback location (like the Desktop or Downloads) so that user simulation data is never lost.

---

## Verification Plan

### Manual Verification
1. Run `python3 setup_env.py` to create the environment and ensure the local virtual environment is created outside the Dropbox directory.
2. Verify that `run.sh` (Mac) and `run.bat` (Windows) are generated successfully.
3. Execute the simulation through the wrapper:
   ```bash
   python3 run_safely.py compass.py --N 4 --M 4 --field_mode forc --forc_n_curves 3 --make_images 1
   ```
4. Verify that the outputs are successfully written to the Dropbox workspace directory without any `PermissionError`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
setup_env.py — Sets up a local, non-synced virtual environment for the compass array simulation.
Creates launcher scripts run.sh/run.bat in the current workspace directory.
"""

import sys
import os
import subprocess
import shutil

def get_venv_dir():
    # Store virtual environment in home directory to avoid syncing thousands of files over Dropbox
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    return os.path.join(home, ".compass_sim_venv")

def check_python_version():
    major, minor = sys.version_info[:2]
    if major < 3 or (major == 3 and minor < 8):
        print(f"Error: Python 3.8+ is required. Detected version: {sys.version}")
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"✓ Detected Python: {sys.version.split()[0]}")

def create_virtual_env(venv_path):
    print(f"\nSetting up virtual environment at: {venv_path}")
    if os.path.exists(venv_path):
        print("✓ Virtual environment directory already exists. Re-verifying packages...")
        return True
    
    try:
        import venv
        venv.create(venv_path, with_pip=True)
        print("✓ Virtual environment created successfully.")
    except ImportError:
        print("Error: The 'venv' module is missing. If on Linux/Ubuntu, install it using: sudo apt install python3-venv")
        sys.exit(1)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error creating virtual environment: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)

def get_venv_pip(venv_path):
    if os.name == 'nt':
        return os.path.join(venv_path, "Scripts", "pip.exe")
    return os.path.join(venv_path, "bin", "pip")

def install_dependencies(venv_path):
    pip_path = get_venv_pip(venv_path)
    requirements_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "requirements.txt")
    
    if not os.path.exists(requirements_path):
        print(f"Error: requirements.txt not found at {requirements_path}")
        sys.exit(1)
        
    print(f"Installing dependencies using {pip_path}...")
    try:
        subprocess.check_call([pip_path, "install", "--upgrade", "pip"])
        subprocess.check_call([pip_path, "install", "-r", requirements_path])
        print("✓ Dependencies installed successfully.")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"Error installing dependencies: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)

def generate_launch_scripts():
    ws_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    
    # macOS/Linux launcher
    sh_content = """#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run.sh — Launcher for the compass simulation environment
VENV_PATH="$HOME/.compass_sim_venv"
if [ ! -d "$VENV_PATH" ]; then
    echo "Error: Virtual environment not found at $VENV_PATH"
    echo "Please run: python3 setup_env.py"
    exit 1
fi
source "$VENV_PATH/bin/activate"
python3 run_safely.py "$@"
"""
    sh_path = os.path.join(ws_dir, "run.sh")
    with open(sh_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(sh_content)
    
    # Try to make run.sh executable on POSIX systems
    if os.name != 'nt':
        try:
            os.chmod(sh_path, 0o755)
            print("✓ Generated run.sh (and marked as executable).")
        except Exception:
            print("✓ Generated run.sh (please run 'chmod +x run.sh' manually).")
    else:
        print("✓ Generated run.sh.")

    # Windows launcher
    bat_content = """@echo off
REM run.bat — Launcher for the compass simulation environment
set VENV_PATH=%USERPROFILE%\\.compass_sim_venv
if not exist "%VENV_PATH%" (
    echo Error: Virtual environment not found at %VENV_PATH%
    echo Please run: python setup_env.py
    exit /b 1
)
call "%VENV_PATH%\\Scripts\\activate.bat"
python run_safely.py %*
"""
    bat_path = os.path.join(ws_dir, "run.bat")
    with open(bat_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(bat_content)
    print("✓ Generated run.bat.")

def main():
    print("==============================================================")
    print("           Compass Simulator Env Setup Tool                   ")
    print("==============================================================")
    
    check_python_version()
    venv_dir = get_venv_dir()
    create_virtual_env(venv_dir)
    install_dependencies(venv_dir)
    generate_launch_scripts()
    
    print("\nEnvironment setup completed successfully!")
    print(f"Virtual environment is at: {venv_dir} (outside Dropbox, not synced)")
    print("To run the code safely on any OS, use the launcher:")
    if os.name == 'nt':
        print("  run.bat compass.py --field_mode forc")
    else:
        print("  ./run.sh compass.py --field_mode forc")
    print("==============================================================")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
run_safely.py — Wrapper script to execute simulation runs in a local temporary folder.
Prevents macOS CloudStorage permission errors (Operation not permitted) and Dropbox file sync locks (Permission denied).
"""

import sys
import os
import subprocess
import shutil
import tempfile
import time

def print_help_and_exit():
    print("Usage: python run_safely.py <script_to_run.py> [arguments...]")
    print("Example: python run_safely.py compass.py --field_mode forc --forc_n_curves 5")
    sys.exit(1)

def get_macos_permission_help():
    return """
========================================================================
[macOS Security Warning] — Operation Not Permitted
------------------------------------------------------------------------
It looks like macOS is blocking this terminal or Python process from
writing directly to the Dropbox folder (~/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox).

To fix this permanently:
1. Open "System Settings" on your Mac.
2. Navigate to "Privacy & Security" -> "Full Disk Access".
3. Add/Toggle on your terminal application (e.g., Terminal, iTerm2,
   or VS Code / Cursor IDE).
4. Restart your terminal application and run the script again.
========================================================================
"""

def get_windows_lock_help():
    return """
========================================================================
[Windows File Lock Warning] — Permission Denied
------------------------------------------------------------------------
It looks like Dropbox or an antivirus scanner is locking the output file
while Python is attempting to write to the shared directory.

To prevent this:
1. Temporarily pause syncing in the Dropbox desktop application before
   running long simulations.
2. Resume syncing when the simulation run completes.
========================================================================
"""

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print_help_and_exit()

    target_script = sys.argv[1]
    script_args = sys.argv[2:]

    if not target_script.endswith(".py"):
        print(f"Error: Target script must be a Python script (.py). Got: '{target_script}'")
        print_help_and_exit()

    orig_dir = os.getcwd()
    target_script_path = os.path.abspath(target_script)

    if not os.path.exists(target_script_path):
        print(f"Error: Script not found: {target_script_path}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # 1. Create a local temporary directory outside of Dropbox
    temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="compass_run_")
    print(f"🚀 Running in local sandboxed directory (non-synced): {temp_dir}")

    # 2. Copy the target script and all helper Python scripts in the same folder to support imports
    py_files_copied = 0
    for file in os.listdir(orig_dir):
        if file.endswith(".py") and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(orig_dir, file)):
            shutil.copy2(os.path.join(orig_dir, file), os.path.join(temp_dir, file))
            py_files_copied += 1
            
    print(f"✓ Copied {py_files_copied} Python source files to local environment.")

    # Record current files in temp_dir before run to detect new outputs
    files_before = set(os.listdir(temp_dir))

    # 3. Build and execute command in temp_dir
    cmd = [sys.executable, target_script] + script_args
    print(f"Executing: {' '.join(cmd)}")
    print("----------------------------------------------------------------")
    
    # Change directory to the local temp directory
    os.chdir(temp_dir)

    process_failed = False
    try:
        # Run process and pipe output in real time
        p = subprocess.Popen(cmd)
        p.wait()
        if p.returncode != 0:
            print(f"\n❌ Process exited with non-zero code: {p.returncode}")
            process_failed = True
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\n■ Run interrupted by user.")
        process_failed = True
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n❌ Error during process execution: {e}")
        process_failed = True

    # 4. Identify generated files
    files_after = set(os.listdir(temp_dir))
    new_files = files_after - files_before

    print("----------------------------------------------------------------")
    if new_files:
        print(f"Found {len(new_files)} new output file(s): {', '.join(new_files)}")
        print(f"Copying files back to Dropbox workspace: {orig_dir}...")
        
        failed_copies = []
        for file in new_files:
            src_file = os.path.join(temp_dir, file)
            dst_file = os.path.join(orig_dir, file)
            try:
                shutil.copy2(src_file, dst_file)
                print(f"  ✓ Copied back: {file}")
            except PermissionError as e:
                failed_copies.append((file, e))
                print(f"  ✗ Failed to copy: {file} ({e})")
            except Exception as e:
                failed_copies.append((file, e))
                print(f"  ✗ Unexpected error copying {file}: {e}")

        # 5. Handle Copy Failures gracefully (Save to fallback directory)
        if failed_copies:
            print("\n⚠️  Some files could not be saved to your Dropbox workspace folder.")
            
            # Setup fallback directory under User's Home folder (Downloads or Desktop)
            fallback_parent = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "Downloads")
            if not os.path.exists(fallback_parent):
                fallback_parent = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "Desktop")
            
            fallback_dir = os.path.join(fallback_parent, "compass_outputs")
            os.makedirs(fallback_dir, exist_ok=True)
            
            print(f"Saving copies to fallback directory instead: {fallback_dir}...")
            
            for file, _ in failed_copies:
                src_file = os.path.join(temp_dir, file)
                dst_file = os.path.join(fallback_dir, file)
                try:
                    shutil.copy2(src_file, dst_file)
                    print(f"  ✓ Saved to fallback: {file}")
                except Exception as ex:
                    print(f"  ✗ Failed fallback save for {file}: {ex}")

            # Explain how to configure their OS to fix the issue
            if sys.platform == 'darwin':
                print(get_macos_permission_help())
            elif os.name == 'nt':
                print(get_windows_lock_help())
            else:
                print(f"Please check write permissions for your Dropbox workspace directory: {orig_dir}")

    else:
        print("No new output files were generated.")

    # 6. Clean up the temp directory
    try:
        shutil.rmtree(temp_dir)
        print("✓ Cleaned up temporary run directory.")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning: Failed to clean up temp directory {temp_dir}: {e}")

    # Return to original working directory
    os.chdir(orig_dir)
    
    if process_failed:
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print("\n✨ Done!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
run_safely.py — Wrapper script to execute simulation runs in a local temporary folder.
Prevents macOS CloudStorage permission errors (Operation not permitted) and Dropbox file sync locks (Permission denied).
"""

import sys
import os
import subprocess
import shutil
import tempfile
import time

def print_help_and_exit():
    print("Usage: python run_safely.py <script_to_run.py> [arguments...]")
    print("Example: python run_safely.py compass.py --field_mode forc --forc_n_curves 5")
    sys.exit(1)

def get_macos_permission_help():
    return """
========================================================================
[macOS Security Warning] — Operation Not Permitted
------------------------------------------------------------------------
It looks like macOS is blocking this terminal or Python process from
writing directly to the Dropbox folder (~/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox).

To fix this permanently:
1. Open "System Settings" on your Mac.
2. Navigate to "Privacy & Security" -> "Full Disk Access".
3. Add/Toggle on your terminal application (e.g., Terminal, iTerm2,
   or VS Code / Cursor IDE).
4. Restart your terminal application and run the script again.
========================================================================
"""

def get_windows_lock_help():
    return """
========================================================================
[Windows File Lock Warning] — Permission Denied
------------------------------------------------------------------------
It looks like Dropbox or an antivirus scanner is locking the output file
while Python is attempting to write to the shared directory.

To prevent this:
1. Temporarily pause syncing in the Dropbox desktop application before
   running long simulations.
2. Resume syncing when the simulation run completes.
========================================================================
"""

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print_help_and_exit()

    target_script = sys.argv[1]
    script_args = sys.argv[2:]

    if not target_script.endswith(".py"):
        print(f"Error: Target script must be a Python script (.py). Got: '{target_script}'")
        print_help_and_exit()

    orig_dir = os.getcwd()
    target_script_path = os.path.abspath(target_script)

    if not os.path.exists(target_script_path):
        print(f"Error: Script not found: {target_script_path}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # 1. Create a local temporary directory outside of Dropbox
    temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="compass_run_")
    print(f"🚀 Running in local sandboxed directory (non-synced): {temp_dir}")

    # 2. Copy the target script and all helper Python scripts in the same folder to support imports
    py_files_copied = 0
    for file in os.listdir(orig_dir):
        if file.endswith(".py") and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(orig_dir, file)):
            shutil.copy2(os.path.join(orig_dir, file), os.path.join(temp_dir, file))
            py_files_copied += 1
            
    print(f"✓ Copied {py_files_copied} Python source files to local environment.")

    # Record current files in temp_dir before run to detect new outputs
    files_before = set(os.listdir(temp_dir))

    # 3. Build and execute command in temp_dir
    cmd = [sys.executable, target_script] + script_args
    print(f"Executing: {' '.join(cmd)}")
    print("----------------------------------------------------------------")
    
    # Change directory to the local temp directory
    os.chdir(temp_dir)

    process_failed = False
    try:
        # Run process and pipe output in real time
        p = subprocess.Popen(cmd)
        p.wait()
        if p.returncode != 0:
            print(f"\n❌ Process exited with non-zero code: {p.returncode}")
            process_failed = True
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\n■ Run interrupted by user.")
        process_failed = True
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n❌ Error during process execution: {e}")
        process_failed = True

    # 4. Identify generated files
    files_after = set(os.listdir(temp_dir))
    new_files = files_after - files_before

    print("----------------------------------------------------------------")
    if new_files:
        print(f"Found {len(new_files)} new output file(s): {', '.join(new_files)}")
        print(f"Copying files back to Dropbox workspace: {orig_dir}...")
        
        failed_copies = []
        for file in new_files:
            src_file = os.path.join(temp_dir, file)
            dst_file = os.path.join(orig_dir, file)
            try:
                shutil.copy2(src_file, dst_file)
                print(f"  ✓ Copied back: {file}")
            except PermissionError as e:
                failed_copies.append((file, e))
                print(f"  ✗ Failed to copy: {file} ({e})")
            except Exception as e:
                failed_copies.append((file, e))
                print(f"  ✗ Unexpected error copying {file}: {e}")

        # 5. Handle Copy Failures gracefully (Save to fallback directory)
        if failed_copies:
            print("\n⚠️  Some files could not be saved to your Dropbox workspace folder.")
            
            # Setup fallback directory under User's Home folder (Downloads or Desktop)
            fallback_parent = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "Downloads")
            if not os.path.exists(fallback_parent):
                fallback_parent = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "Desktop")
            
            fallback_dir = os.path.join(fallback_parent, "compass_outputs")
            os.makedirs(fallback_dir, exist_ok=True)
            
            print(f"Saving copies to fallback directory instead: {fallback_dir}...")
            
            for file, _ in failed_copies:
                src_file = os.path.join(temp_dir, file)
                dst_file = os.path.join(fallback_dir, file)
                try:
                    shutil.copy2(src_file, dst_file)
                    print(f"  ✓ Saved to fallback: {file}")
                except Exception as ex:
                    print(f"  ✗ Failed fallback save for {file}: {ex}")

            # Explain how to configure their OS to fix the issue
            if sys.platform == 'darwin':
                print(get_macos_permission_help())
            elif os.name == 'nt':
                print(get_windows_lock_help())
            else:
                print(f"Please check write permissions for your Dropbox workspace directory: {orig_dir}")

    else:
        print("No new output files were generated.")

    # 6. Clean up the temp directory
    try:
        shutil.rmtree(temp_dir)
        print("✓ Cleaned up temporary run directory.")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning: Failed to clean up temp directory {temp_dir}: {e}")

    # Return to original working directory
    os.chdir(orig_dir)
    
    if process_failed:
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print("\n✨ Done!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

To solve write access restrictions and file locks inside Dropbox across macOS, Windows, and Linux, we implemented a full environment wrapper suite:

### 1. Non-Synced Virtual Environment Setup
- Created [requirements.txt](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/requirements.txt) to define core dependencies (`numpy` and `matplotlib`).
- Created [setup_env.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/setup_env.py) which builds a local virtual environment stored outside the Dropbox directory (at `~/.compass_sim_venv`). This prevents syncing thousands of pip files over Dropbox and eliminates cross-platform path/binary incompatibility.
- Automatically generated OS-specific launcher scripts in the workspace directory:
  - [run.sh](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/run.sh) (for macOS/Linux)

*   **Lattice**: 10x10 Honeycomb geometry (which has a coordination number of 3, leading to fascinating collective switching dynamics).
*   **Saturation Field**: $B_{sat} = 80\text{ mT}$ (`--B_ext 0.08`).
*   **Curves**: 35 curves (`--forc_n_curves 35`) to capture fine-grained reversal points.

The issue preventing the video from generating has been fixed. 

### Why did it happen?
When generating double-panel figures (needles on the left, $M \times H$ curves on the right), Matplotlib dynamically crops white margins. This dynamic cropping frequently results in odd pixel dimensions (e.g. height or width of 721 pixels). The H.264 video encoder used by `ffmpeg` strictly requires dimensions to be divisible by 2, which caused it to fail with `height not divisible by 2` errors and abort the video generation.

### The Fix
I updated the video compiler function in [compass.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/compass.py) (and the frozen copy [compass_simV68.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/compass_simV68.py)) to use the robust `scale=trunc(iw/2)*2:trunc(ih/2)*2` filter and ordered it correctly in the `ffmpeg` pipeline. This forces even dimensions regardless of the figure size or crop, making the video generation work seamlessly for both the **hysteresis** and **forc** strategies.

---

You can now run this directly to generate the side-by-side video:

```bash
python3 compass.py --field_mode forc --video honeycomb_forc --forc_n_curves 15 --damping 8e-6
```

def _plot_hysteresis(log, hyst_autoscale=False, forc_sweep='both'):
    is_forc = False
    if isinstance(log, list) and len(log) > 0 and len(log[0]) == 7:
        is_forc = True
    elif isinstance(log, np.ndarray) and log.ndim == 2 and log.shape[1] == 7:
        is_forc = True

    if is_forc:
        t_arr = np.array([row[0] for row in log], dtype=float)
        B_arr = np.array([row[1] for row in log], dtype=float) * 1e3
        M_arr = np.array([row[2] for row in log], dtype=float)
    else:
        log_arr = np.array(log, dtype=float)
        t_arr  = log_arr[:, 0]
        B_arr  = log_arr[:, 1] * 1e3
        M_arr  = log_arr[:, 2]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5), facecolor='#1A1A2E')

    ax1 = axes[0]
    ax1.set_facecolor('#0D1B2A')
    
    if is_forc:
        from collections import defaultdict
        segments = defaultdict(list)
        for row in log:
            if forc_sweep == 'up' and row[5] != 'up':
                continue
            if forc_sweep == 'down' and row[5] != 'down':
                continue
            if forc_sweep == 'both' and row[5] not in ('up', 'down'):
                continue
            segments[int(row[6])].append(row)
        
        for k_val in sorted(segments.keys()):
            arr_seg = np.array(segments[k_val])
            H_seg = arr_seg[:, 1].astype(float) * 1e3
            M_seg = arr_seg[:, 2].astype(float)
            ax1.plot(H_seg, M_seg, color='#E94560', lw=1.2, alpha=0.85)
    else:
        ax1.plot(B_arr, M_arr, color='#E94560', lw=1.2, alpha=0.85)

    ax1.axhline(0, color='#4A4A6A', lw=0.6, ls='--')
    ax1.axvline(0, color='#4A4A6A', lw=0.6, ls='--')
    ax1.set_xlabel("Field B [mT]",    color='#BDC3C7')
    ax1.set_ylabel("Magnetization M (projection)",  color='#BDC3C7')
    if is_forc:
        ax1.set_title("FORC Curves M x B", color='#ECF0F1', fontfamily='monospace')
    else:
        ax1.set_title("Hysteresis Loop M x B", color='#ECF0F1', fontfamily='monospace')
    ax1.tick_params(colors='#7F8C8D')
    ax1.grid(True, color='#2C3E50', alpha=0.5)
    for sp in ax1.spines.values():
        sp.set_edgecolor('#2C3E50')

    if not hyst_autoscale:
        if is_forc:
            if forc_sweep == 'up':
                filtered_rows = [row for row in log if row[5] == 'up']
            elif forc_sweep == 'down':
                filtered_rows = [row for row in log if row[5] == 'down']
            else:
                filtered_rows = [row for row in log if row[5] in ('up', 'down')]

def _plot_hysteresis(log, hyst_autoscale=False):
    log = np.array(log)
    is_forc = (log.ndim == 2 and log.shape[1] == 7)

    t_arr  = log[:, 0]
    B_arr  = log[:, 1] * 1e3
    M_arr  = log[:, 2]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5), facecolor='#1A1A2E')

    ax1 = axes[0]
    ax1.set_facecolor('#0D1B2A')
    
    if is_forc:
        from collections import defaultdict
        segments = defaultdict(list)
        for row in log:
            if row[5]:  # is_up_sweep
                segments[int(row[6])].append(row)
        
        for k_val in sorted(segments.keys()):
            arr_seg = np.array(segments[k_val])
            H_seg = arr_seg[:, 1] * 1e3
            M_seg = arr_seg[:, 2]
            ax1.plot(H_seg, M_seg, color='#E94560', lw=1.2, alpha=0.85)
    else:
        ax1.plot(B_arr, M_arr, color='#E94560', lw=1.2, alpha=0.85)

    ax1.axhline(0, color='#4A4A6A', lw=0.6, ls='--')
    ax1.axvline(0, color='#4A4A6A', lw=0.6, ls='--')

        ax1.set_title("FORC Curves M x B", color='#ECF0F1', fontfamily='monospace')
    else:
        ax1.set_title("Hysteresis Loop M x B", color='#ECF0F1', fontfamily='monospace')
    ax1.tick_params(colors='#7F8C8D')
    ax1.grid(True, color='#2C3E50', alpha=0.5)
    for sp in ax1.spines.values():
        sp.set_edgecolor('#2C3E50')

    if not hyst_autoscale:
        if is_forc:
            up_sweep_rows = [row for row in log if row[5]]

                B_arr_for_lim = arr_up[:, 1] * 1e3
            else:
                B_arr_for_lim = B_arr
        else:
            B_arr_for_lim = B_arr
            
        B_max = np.max(np.abs(B_arr_for_lim))

            B_max = 1.0
        ax1.set_xlim(-1.05 * B_max, 1.05 * B_max)
        ax1.set_ylim(-1.15, 1.15)

    ax2 = axes[1]

    ax2b.tick_params(colors='#FFD700')
    ax2.set_xlabel("Physical time t [s]", color='#BDC3C7')

    ax2.set_title("Time evolution", color='#ECF0F1', fontfamily='monospace')
    ax2.tick_params(colors='#7F8C8D')
    ax2.grid(True, color='#2C3E50', alpha=0.4)
    for sp in ax2.spines.values():
        sp.set_edgecolor('#2C3E50')
    lines = [l1, plt.Line2D([0],[0], color='#FFD700', ls='--')]
    ax2.legend(lines, ['M (proj.)', 'B (mT)'], facecolor='#1A1A2E',
               edgecolor='#2C3E50', labelcolor='#ECF0F1', fontsize=8)

    if is_forc:

    else:
        fig.suptitle("Magnetic Hysteresis Simulation — Compass Array",
                     color='#BDC3C7', fontsize=12, fontfamily='monospace')
                     
    plt.tight_layout()
    out_img = "forc_curves.png" if is_forc else "hysteresis_loop.png"

I have added the `--forc_sweep` option to control which parts of the First-Order Reversal Curves (FORCs) are traced, exported, and plotted. The version of the simulation script has been bumped to **V69**.

### New Parameter Details
*   **`--forc_sweep`** (choices: `both`, `up`, `down`; default: `both`):
    *   `both` (default): Traces, logs, and plots **both** the down-sweeps (decreasing field) and up-sweeps (increasing field) for each reversal branch, creating complete reversal loops.
    *   `up`: Logs and plots only the up-sweeps (increasing field sweep back to positive saturation). This corresponds to the V68 behavior.
    *   `down`: Logs and plots only the down-sweeps (decreasing field sweep from saturation down to the reversal field $B_r$).

The CSV data export (e.g. `forc_curve.csv`), the real-time video frames (in `axR`), and the final summary plot (`forc_curves.png`) all respect this setting and filter the data accordingly.

### Files Updated
1.  [compass.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/compass.py) (V69): Core simulation logic, plots, argparse, and CSV export.
2.  [freeze_v69.py](file:///Users/jps/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/simula%20agulhas/freeze_v69.py) (NEW): Frozen snapshot launcher for V69.

### Examples of Direct python3 execution:
*   To trace and save/plot **both** sweep directions (default):
    ```bash
    python3 compass.py --field_mode forc --forc_n_curves 30 --forc_sweep both
    ```
*   To trace **only the up-sweep** (increasing field):
    ```bash
    python3 compass.py --field_mode forc --forc_n_curves 30 --forc_sweep up
    ```
*   To trace **only the down-sweep** (decreasing field):
    ```bash
    python3 compass.py --field_mode forc --forc_n_curves 30 --forc_sweep down
    ```

You can run `python3 freeze_v69.py` in your terminal to create the frozen copy `compass_simV69.py` from `compass.py` at any time.

**`pyrefly init`** is a command-line utility used to initialize or configure the **Pyrefly** type checker within a Python project[1][2].

### What `pyrefly init` Does
*   **Creates Configuration:** It generates a `pyrefly.toml` file in your project root or updates your existing `pyproject.toml` file with a `[tool.pyrefly]` section[3][4].
*   **Migrates Existing Settings:** If it detects an existing configuration from other type checkers like **Mypy** (e.g., `mypy.ini` or `[tool.mypy]` in `pyproject.toml`) or **Pyright**, it will attempt to migrate those settings into the Pyrefly format[3][5][6].
*   **Initial Verification:** The command typically triggers an initial type-check run to ensure the configuration is set up correctly and to identify any immediate issues in the project[7][2].

### Usage
To initialize Pyrefly in your project, navigate to your project's root directory in your terminal and run[5][2]:
```bash
pyrefly init
```

### Context: What is Pyrefly?
Pyrefly is a high-performance, open-source **static type checker and language server** for Python, developed by Meta[8][9][10]. It is designed for speed—capable of checking millions of lines of code per second—and provides standard IDE features like code navigation, autocomplete, and semantic highlighting[8][11][12].

```bash

```

604: \noindent\textbf{(7) forc} --- First-Order Reversal Curve (FORC) suite. The system simulates a complete family of first-order reversal curves. Each cycle saturates the array at $+B_{\max}$, ramps down to a reversal field $B_{r, k}$ (spaced evenly from $+B_{\max}$ to the minimum reversal field \code{--forc\_Br\_min}), and sweeps back to $+B_{\max}$. The sweep is repeated for a total of \code{--forc\_n\_curves} cycles. Timing is automatically calculated so that the total time is $t_{\mathrm{sim}} = N_{\mathrm{curves}} \cdot (t_{\mathrm{sat}} + t_{\mathrm{ramp\_down}} + t_{\mathrm{ramp\_up}})$. The entire suite of curves is logged to \code{forc\_curve.csv} containing the reversal field $B_r$ as a fifth column:
605: \begin{verbatim}
606: # Run a family of 30 FORC curves, sweeping Br down to -5 mT
607: python3 compass.py --N 20 --M 20 --field_mode forc \
608:     --ext_Bx 0.005 --forc_Br_min -0.005 --forc_n_curves 30
609: \end{verbatim}
610: 
611: \noindent In \code{hysteresis}, the $M(B)$ loop is exported to \code{hysteresis\_loop.csv}; in \code{forc}, to \code{forc\_curve.csv}; in \code{sine}, to \code{sine\_field.csv}. In pulse/step modes, \code{--torque\_tol} controls the equilibrium criterion and \code{--t\_sim\_full 1} disables early stopping (Appendix~A).
612: 
613: \subsection*{B.8 --- Magnetic-domain visualization}
614:

**Implementing Demag Procedure**

I'm currently working on implementing the `demag` procedure within the `compass.py` code. The core functionality involves a sinusoidal field sweep, oscillating from +B_etx down to zero, and then through negative values. A key element is a 30% field reduction per cycle. I need to ensure this is implemented precisely to match the desired demagnetization profile.


**Defining Demag Equation**

I've been working to formalize the demagnetization equation. It's becoming clear that an exponential decay envelope, $B(t) = B_{ext} \cdot 0.7^{f_{demag} \cdot t} \cdot \cos(2\pi f_{demag} t)$, accurately reflects the 30% reduction per cycle, and also provides a smooth transition to zero, through negative values. This aligns precisely with the design specifications for the AFD procedure. I feel confident this is the appropriate expression.


**Determining Demag Duration**

I've realized the elegance of separating the simulation into demagnetization and main phases. The demag phase runs until the field amplitude is practically zero. I'm exploring the best way to define the demag duration, leaning towards a fixed number of cycles, possibly configurable via a `--demag_cycles` parameter, defaulting to 20 or 30 cycles. This approach will give complete control over the total simulation time, which is just the sum of the demag time and the main simulation time. This will also give good control over the simulation parameters.


**Implementing Demag Parameters**

I've just added the parameters to enable and control the demagnetization phase. There's a `--demag` flag, defaulting to 'off', with `--demag_freq` defaulting to 2.0 Hz, and `--demag_cycles` defaulting to 20. The demagnetization's duration will be calculated based on these parameters. This also includes the implementation for adjusting the external field function.


**Analyzing External Field Strength**

I'm now focusing on how the demagnetization field interacts with `B_ext`. I've determined that `B_max`, calculated within the `relax()` function, precisely represents the amplitude of the external field, regardless of how the user defines it. This means I can reliably use `B_max` as the initial amplitude for the demagnetization field. I also realized that if B_ext is 0, the demag field will also be 0, which is normal.


**Calculating Total Simulation Time**

I've just refined the simulation time calculations. I am setting the total simulation time, `t_sim_total`, as the sum of the main simulation time (`t_sim`) and the demagnetization time (`t_demag`).  Then, the total number of simulation steps is calculated based on `t_sim_total` and the time step, `dt`. I've also verified that the existing `field_at(t)` function in all modes can be implemented using an offset to account for `t_demag`, and that this requires almost no modifications to the rest of the code!


**Verifying Logged Time**

I'm now focusing on how the time variable, `t_now`, works, specifically concerning the simulation logs. I've confirmed that `t_now` starts at `dt` and runs to `t_sim_total`, which means it encompasses both the demagnetization and main simulation phases. The current question I am pondering is whether or not we should include the demagnetization phase in the output CSV files.


**Refining Log Output Logic**

I'm now implementing the new output logging system. The goal is to isolate the data related to the demagnetization and main phases. I've realized that the demagnetization should be considered an initial state preparation phase. Hence, to keep the output CSVs clean, I'll log data to `hysteresis_log`, `sine_log`, and `field_log` *only* when the simulation time, `t_now`, is greater than or equal to the demagnetization time, `t_demag`. This approach will ensure that the exported data accurately represents the measurement phase, starting at time 0. This gives clean and precise data plots!


**Deciding Video Inclusion**

I'm now determining the video frame and logging behavior. I've realized there are pros and cons to showing the demagnetization phase in the video and plots. I'm leaning toward keeping the logging of data (and video frames) restricted to $t_{now} \ge t_{demag}$ by default. But, I am considering the elegant approach of shifting the logged time so the main simulation starts at $t_{local} = 0$, with negative times for the demag phase ($t_{logged} = t_{now} - t_{demag}$). However, I am concerned about compatibility with analysis scripts. Therefore, to ensure that the plots are easy to work with, it may be better **not to log** that initial phase.


**Confirming Demag Time Exclusion**

I've carefully considered the implications of including the demagnetization phase in the logged data and video output. By restricting logging and video frames to $t_{now} \ge t_{demag}$, the data starts at precisely time zero, compatible with all analysis scripts. The demagnetization itself is handled as a pretreatment. This ensures a clean data stream and seamless integration with existing analysis workflows.

605: \noindent\textbf{(7) forc} --- First-Order Reversal Curve (FORC) suite. The system simulates a complete family of first-order reversal curves. Each cycle saturates the array at $+B_{\max}$, ramps down to a reversal field $B_{r, k}$ (spaced evenly from $+B_{\max}$ to the minimum reversal field \code{--forc\_Br\_min}), and sweeps back to $+B_{\max}$. The sweep is repeated for a total of \code{--forc\_n\_curves} cycles. Timing is automatically calculated so that the total time is $t_{\mathrm{sim}} = N_{\mathrm{curves}} \cdot (t_{\mathrm{sat}} + t_{\mathrm{ramp\_down}} + t_{\mathrm{ramp\_up}})$. The parameter \code{--forc\_sweep} (\code{both}, \code{up}, or \code{down}; V69) controls which sweep branches (decreasing, increasing, or both) are logged and plotted. The entire suite of curves is logged to \code{forc\_curve.csv} containing the reversal field $B_r$ as a fifth column:

607: # Run a family of 30 FORC curves, tracing both branches, sweeping Br down to -5 mT
608: python3 compass.py --N 20 --M 20 --field_mode forc \
609:     --ext_Bx 0.005 --forc_Br_min -0.005 --forc_n_curves 30 --forc_sweep both

\paragraph{Simulator capabilities (current state, V70).}
The simulator supports three lattice geometries (square, triangular, honeycomb); \textbf{seven} external-field modes: static; First-Order Reversal Curve (FORC) mode with sat/reversal field parameter control; pulse with explicit timing (delay $\Delta t$ $\to$ field for $t_{\mathrm{pulse}}$ $\to$ zero field until equilibrium, with the legacy saturation/plateau criterion if $t_{\mathrm{pulse}}$ is not given); five-segment hysteresis ($0 \to +B \to 0 \to -B \to 0 \to +B$) with linear or log-symmetric spacing; sinusoidal field; and step modes \code{step\_pos} ($B{=}0$ for $\Delta t$, then field kept on) and \code{step\_neg} (field from $t{=}0$, removed at $\Delta t$). Additionally, a sinusoidal decaying demagnetization procedure (\code{--demag on}) can be enabled before any field mode. It also supports periodic boundary conditions with lattice images; real-time monitoring of the alignment order parameter $S \in [0,1]$; a real-equilibrium criterion (small angular velocity \emph{and} small mean torque) for pulse/step modes; optional GPU backend through CuPy; MP4 video export, summary images, and CSV time series $(t, B, M, S)$; magnetic-domain visualization through halo coloring; a precomputed dipolar tensor (V40); and performance instrumentation.

\item \textbf{FORC protocol implementation (V67)}: introduction of the First-Order Reversal Curve (FORC) field mode (\code{forc}) with saturation/reversal field parameter control (\code{--forc\_Br}, \code{--forc\_t\_sat}, \code{--forc\_t\_rev}), real-time dual-panel video monitoring of the minor reversal loop, and automated export to \code{forc\_curve.csv}.
